Advances: specled.package

From the specled_-vk0 test-quality gate (epic specled_-233, 2026-07-26). Both are FALSE NEGATIVES in the stale-allow-marker sweep that specled_-vk0 ADDED — limitations of new work in that PR, not inherited debt. Neither was blocking: they weaken a new supplementary check, they do not cause a false pass of the main doc-identifier lint, and the sweep does catch both rot directions on well-formed markers (proved by data-level mutations against the live ADR corpus).

Both confirmed by probe in `test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs`.

## HOLE 1 — a `>` in the reason text defeats the comment strip

`@allow_marker_comment_pattern` (:168) uses `[^>]*` to match the marker comment, so the first `>` inside the reason text terminates the match early and the marker is never stripped. Confirmed by probe with this marker:

    <!-- spec-lint:allow-code=branch_guard_fake see A > B -->

The marker is left unstripped, so the in-marker token itself counts as a token "outside the marker", and rot direction (b) — "the marker's token no longer appears on its line" — cannot fire. A stale marker whose reason contains a `>` is permanently exempt and invisible to the sweep.

## HOLE 2 — grammar asymmetry between the two marker patterns

`@allow_marker_pattern` (:167) does NOT require the `<!-- -->` wrapper, so the MAIN lint honours a bare marker of the form `spec-lint:allow-code=<token>` sitting in plain prose. But only WRAPPED markers are stripped by `@allow_marker_comment_pattern` (:168).

Net effect: a bare unwrapped marker grants a real exemption in the enforcement path while being structurally invisible to the staleness sweep — the exact "permanent unearned exemption" shape that specled_-vk0's stale-marker item was filed to close. Confirmed by probe.

## Fix

Make the two patterns share one grammar. Either require the wrapper in both (and reject bare markers in the main lint), or strip on the marker token itself rather than on the surrounding HTML comment. Then add a regression test per hole: a marker whose reason contains `>` must still be strippable, and a bare unwrapped marker must be either rejected by the main lint or visible to the sweep.

Verify each by falsification before committing — remove the fix and confirm the new test goes RED. (Epic specled_-233 lesson: run the falsifiability gate against the specific clause you strengthened, not a convenient one.)

## Also from the same review — smaller items, same file

- `:426` (the stale-marker corpus sweep) has NO corpus-size guard, unlike its siblings at `:233` (asserts `> 50` files) and `:254` (asserts `> 8` files), which exist precisely so a repo reorg or cwd change cannot silently no-op the lint. `decision_files()` has no equivalent, so an empty decision-file glob would pass silently. `:266` partly covers this by asserting `.spec/` appears, but not `.spec/decisions/` specifically.

- `:360`'s failure message says "dead in @known_codes" when the likeliest real cause is a stale `@implementation_code_files` (a new lib file emitting codes that was never added to the list). The implied action reads as "delete the entry", which is wrong. Self-correcting — deleting a real code trips the docs scan at `:243` — but the message misleads. Measured blast radius: dropping `append_only.ex`, `evidence/store.ex`, `overlap.ex`, or `spec.check.ex` from the list reports 0 differences, because their codes are all mirrored in `branch_check.ex`; only a rename-induced ENOENT catches those four.

- `:510`'s message is imprecise for a marker naming an unguarded bare code (e.g. `allow-code=detector_unavailable`): it reports "that token does not appear outside the marker on the same line" even when it plainly does, because `guarded_tokens/1` only matches the five guarded families. The verdict (remove the unnecessary marker) is right; only the stated reason is wrong. No such marker exists today.

- `:269` pins ONE live spec file by name (`.spec/specs/prose_guard.spec.md:83`) as its atom-form-severity example. Two others carry the same shape (`branch_guard.spec.md:338`, `spec_drift_trailer.spec.md:80`), so asserting any-of-`.spec/**` would survive a reword of that one scenario's `given:` clause. Failure would be loud and the path is visible in ExUnit's printed expression, so it misleads no one — it just breaks more often than necessary.

- `fixture_file/1` (:556) writes into a FIXED shared directory with a VM-local-counter filename. This is permitted for test-only paths under `specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names`, and the filename is not fixed, so it is NOT a significant flake risk. Residual sliver: two concurrent VMs can emit the same `System.unique_integer` value, and VM B's `on_exit` `File.rm` could delete VM A's fixture between write and read. The window is microseconds and the content is identical at the single call site. Folding `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` into the DIRECTORY name would close it entirely.

ADMISSION VERIFICATION (specled_-k6s, 2026-07-27)
Cold fresh-context verifier run against the epic base tree (feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors @ e81f9f98).

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: medium
Mandate confirmed still applicable as written; no narrowing needed.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
ALL of it. Single file: test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs.

1. Unify the two marker grammars (:167-168) so they cannot drift. Recommended end state — derive both from one wrapper-required grammar:
   - `@allow_marker_comment_pattern` must use a lazy any-char body instead of `[^>]*`, e.g. `~r{<!--\s*spec-lint:allow-code=[a-z_/]+.*?-->}` so a reason containing `>` still strips.
   - `@allow_marker_pattern` must require the `<!-- ... -->` wrapper and capture the token, e.g. `~r{<!--\s*spec-lint:allow-code=([a-z_/]+).*?-->}`, so `allowed_codes/1` (:469) no longer honours a bare unwrapped marker. (The alternative sanctioned by the ticket — strip on the marker token itself rather than the surrounding comment — is acceptable, but then the sweep must still see bare markers.)
   Keep both single-line-scoped: the corpus is streamed line-by-line via `File.stream!/1` (:238, :485), so `.*?` cannot span lines in practice, but do not add the `s` modifier.

2. Add two REGRESSION tests, each falsified before commit (revert the fix, confirm RED):
   a. `stale_allow_marker_violations([{"<!-- spec-lint:allow-code=branch_guard_totally_made_up see A > B -->", @decision_file, 1}])` must equal the `...but that token does not appear outside the marker on the same line` violation. Today it returns `[]`.
   b. Bare-marker test: `unknown_tokens("a `branch_guard_totally_made_up` code spec-lint:allow-code=branch_guard_totally_made_up no wrapper", @decision_file)` must equal `["branch_guard_totally_made_up"]` (rejected by the main lint). Today it returns `[]`. If instead the "visible to the sweep" arm is chosen, assert the sweep reports it.

3. Corpus-size guard on the sweep test (:422-429): add `files = decision_files()`, `assert length(files) > N, "decision corpus collapsed to ... — the sweep is a no-op"` (there are 12+ files under .spec/decisions/ today; pick a conservative N and state it), and optionally `assert Enum.all?(files, &String.starts_with?(&1, ".spec/decisions/"))`.

4. Reword the mirror failure message (:360-363) so the "dead in @known_codes" side also names the likelier cause: a stale `@implementation_code_files` (:184-195) missing a new lib file that emits the code. The implied action must not read as "delete the entry".

5. Split the :510 branch: when `code` is not matched by any `@token_patterns` family (i.e. `Regex.match?(@guarded_code_shape, code)` is false, :181), emit a distinct message ("allow-marker names <code>, which is not in a guarded family — the marker is unnecessary") rather than the false "does not appear outside the marker" claim.

6. Broaden :269: replace the single-file pin `atom_severity_offenders([".spec/specs/prose_guard.spec.md"]) != []` with an any-of assertion over `Path.wildcard(".spec/specs/*.spec.md")` (or the three known-shape files), so a reword of one scenario's `given:` clause does not break the test.

7. `fixture_file/1` (:556-563): fold `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` into the DIRECTORY name, e.g. `Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "specled_docs_identifier_lint_test_#{SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix()}")`, and reword the ADR reference to the current `specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach` (the ticket cites the superseded `specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names`).

Optional spec touch: .spec/specs/package.spec.md:113 says only "carries an explicit `spec-lint:allow-code=<token>` marker on the same line" — it does not mandate the `<!-- -->` wrapper. If option (1a) is taken, tighten that clause to name the wrapped form, matching the moduledoc at :67-72.

== EXPECTED TOUCHES ==
test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs, .spec/specs/package.spec.md

== RISK NOTES ==
REALIZATION HASH: none. `.spec/realization_hashes.json` contains exactly one top-level key, `api_boundary`, and `grep -c "specled.package"` over it returns 0. No realized_by binding names test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs. Editing this file cannot trip the realization-drift gate.

GATE COUPLING: .spec/specs/package.spec.md:120-127 verifies `specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity` via `kind: tagged_tests, execute: true`. Every test in this file carries `@tag spec: "specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity"`. So a regex mistake here fails bare `mix spec.check`, not just `mix test`. The `--no-run-commands` form will NOT catch it — full `mix spec.check` (or at minimum `mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs`) is required before this ticket is called done.

HARD CONFLICT — specled_-4pl edits the SAME FILE at overlapping regions and must be sequenced with this one (same-file, same-attribute-block): its mandate names moduledoc :44 ("Deferred to specled_-vk0"), the `@token_patterns` comment :155-156, `@known_code_list` :139 (dead indirection to delete), `@implementation_code_files` :184-195, and the mirror test at :357-364 — which is literally ozm's smaller item #4 (the "dead in @known_codes" message). Decide ONE owner for the :357-364 message rewording or the two tickets will produce competing edits. 4pl also edits .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md, which is one of the four live marker-bearing ADRs this ticket's sweep reads (lines :22, :24, :47) — if 4pl rewrites those lines, re-run the sweep after both land.

CONFLICT — specled_-ehv is a repo-wide sweep of the 30 test files that combine `System.tmp_dir!()` with `unique_integer`; test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:556-563 is one of them. ozm item #7 and ehv would edit the same 8 lines. Prefer letting ehv own the mechanical sweep and dropping item #7 from ozm, or vice versa — but not both.

SOFT — specled_-26g is the same temp-name defect class in a different file (evidence Store.read_status sidecar tests); no textual overlap, but it should adopt the same `cross_vm_suffix/0`-in-directory-name shape for consistency.

SOFT — specled_-yds edits test/docs_concepts_content_lint_test.exs (different file) but cites test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:298 as precedent and advances the same subject (specled.package), so both land under the same tagged_tests verification entry. specled_-z5t also advances specled.package but edits skills/spec-led-bootstrap/references/adoption-phases.md — note that skills/** IS inside this lint's `finding_code_corpus/0` (:216), so a z5t edit that introduces a finding-code-shaped token would be caught by this test.

DEPENDENCY: none blocking. This ticket is self-contained and needs no other ticket to land first; only the 4pl/ehv ordering decisions above.

FALSIFIABILITY MANDATE: the ticket explicitly requires proving each new test RED by reverting the specific clause strengthened (epic specled_-233 lesson). An implementer that only reports "tests pass" has not satisfied the ticket.

SCOPE CONTRACT (orchestrator, specled_-k6s — 2026-07-27)

Authoritative for mechanical scope checks. Supplements, does not replace, the
ADMISSION VERIFICATION comment's mandate (items 1-7), which is what you implement.

## LINE NUMBERS HAVE MOVED — match by content
specled_-4pl has ALREADY LANDED on the epic branch and edited this same file
(`test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs`): it inlined `@known_code_list` into
`@known_codes` and reworded two comments. Every line number the admission comment cites
has shifted by roughly one. Your stage is cut from the current epic head, so you have
4pl's version. Re-read the file and anchor on CONTENT, never on the cited line numbers.

specled_-ehv has also landed. Its amended
`.spec/decisions/specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach.md` is the current ADR —
item 7 is already aligned with it (fold `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` into the
directory name, and reference `cross_vm_temp_names_reach`, not the superseded
`cross_vm_temp_names`).

## Allowed touches
- `test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs`
- `.spec/specs/package.spec.md` — the OPTIONAL item only: if you take option (1a) and
  require the `<!-- -->` wrapper, tighten the clause that currently says only "carries
  an explicit `spec-lint:allow-code=<token>` marker on the same line" so it names the
  wrapped form. Spec co-change is AUTHORIZED for this. It is append-only-checked:
  tighten in place, never delete or downgrade.

## Out of Scope (files)
- `lib/**` — no production change. The lint lives entirely in the test file.
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md` — specled_-4pl
  owns it and has landed. Do not touch it, and do NOT disturb its two
  `<!-- spec-lint:allow-code=... -->` markers, which your own sweep depends on.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (orchestrator consolidates once at the end), `VERSION`,
  `.spec/realization_hashes.json`, `.spec/state.json`.
- Every file not listed under Allowed touches.

## Out of Scope (intent)
- Keep both marker grammars SINGLE-LINE-SCOPED. The corpus is streamed line-by-line via
  `File.stream!/1`, so `.*?` cannot span lines in practice — but do NOT add the `s`
  modifier, which would change that.
- Do not implement specled_-4pl's FINDING 2 (union → per-emitting-site) or guard
  `@implementation_code_files` staleness. Both were explicitly descoped there and are
  not yours. Item 4 only REWORDS the mirror failure message to name the likelier cause;
  it does not change the mirror's logic.
- No new dependencies.

## FALSIFIABILITY BAR — this ticket is one of the five the epic gates on
This ticket fixes two evasion holes in a lint. A fix whose regression tests cannot fail
is the same defect one level up. For BOTH item-2 tests:
1. Write the test, confirm it is GREEN with your fix in place.
2. REVERT the grammar fix, confirm the test goes RED, and paste the failure.
3. Restore the fix, confirm green.
Record both mutations and their reverts in the COMMIT MESSAGE. "Tests pass" is not
evidence here — today both cases return `[]`, which is exactly why the holes survived.

Item 3's corpus-size guard must also be shown to work: state the N you chose, the actual
file count, and why N is conservative.

## Verification (change-scoped, run-until-green; host mix, no compose)
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs` — every test must stay green, including
   the pre-existing 16.
3. `mix format --check-formatted`
4. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`

Do NOT run bare `mix spec.check` and do NOT run the full suite. The orchestrator owns
whole-system proof at the merge gate and PR CI.

  (f) FOUR LIVE MARKERS: yes, all four still honoured. I enumerated every marker-bearing line in the live corpus under the NEW grammar and printed the exemption set and unknown-token set per line:
      .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md:22 exempts=["branch_guard_test_only_change"] unknown=[]
      .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md:24 exempts=["branch_guard_missing_subject_update_attested"] unknown=[]
      .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md:47 exempts=[] unknown=[]   (literal template line — correctly inert)
      .spec/decisions/specled.decision.file_touch_yields_to_realization.md:108 exempts=["branch_guard_missing_subject_update_attested"] unknown=[]
      .spec/decisions/specled.decision.finding_code_budget.md:47 exempts=["branch_guard_test_only_change"] unknown=[]
    Full-corpus sweep over all 51 decision files: violations == []. The wrapper requirement rejects no real marker.

  TREE LEFT CLEAN: yes. All temporary mutations (grammar revert; three spec.md mutations described below) were reverted with `git checkout --`. Final `git status --short` shows only the untracked `.grok/sandbox.toml` I was told to ignore, and `git diff --stat` against HEAD is empty. Probe copies live only in the session scratchpad, never in the repo.

- Spec-edit append-only check (step 10): PASS by inspection AND by mutation.
  The `.spec/specs/package.spec.md` diff is ONE line: the clause "carries an explicit `spec-lint:allow-code=<token>` marker on the same line" becomes "carries an explicit `<!-- spec-lint:allow-code=<token> reason -->` marker on the same line". The requirement `id`, `priority: must` and `stability: stable` are byte-identical; no requirement, scenario, or verification entry is deleted; nothing else in the file changed. This TIGHTENS the clause in place and matches the new grammar and the moduledoc.
  I also mutated the file three times to test the gate: (1) `priority: must` -> `should` — spec.check still passed; (2) statement "shall" -> "may" — spec.check still passed; (3) deleting the whole `specled.package.declarative_governance` requirement — spec.check FAILED (`result=fail tier=validate`). So a deletion IS mechanically caught. See Notes for the (1)/(2) observation. All three reverted.

- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)
- Audit-expanded scope, if any: none. specled_-ozm carries three comments (ADMISSION VERIFICATION, SCOPE CONTRACT, IMPLEMENTED); there is no `AUDIT: BOUNCE` comment, so no file outside the Allowed globs is in scope.

Verdict: PASS

Notes (advisory only, nothing blocking):
1. PRE-EXISTING INFRA, NOT THIS DIFF — the `append_only` leg appears not to fire for spec statement/priority changes under `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` against `origin/main`. Mutating `priority: must` -> `should`, and separately the modal verb `shall` -> `may`, on `specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity` each produced `spec.check result=pass` with zero `append_only/*` findings (not even `append_only/no_baseline`). `BranchCheck.contract_findings/4` does call `AppendOnly.analyze` and `append_only_applicable?` is true here (real git repo, base != "HEAD"), so the likely cause is `fetch_prior_state/2` having no committed baseline — `.spec/state.json` is gitignored per CLAUDE.md. Requirement DELETION is still caught, but via the validate leg (dangling `covers:` reference), not via `append_only/requirement_deleted`. This is exactly the "gate that cannot fail" class the epic cares about; worth a separate ticket. It does NOT affect this verdict — ozm's spec edit deletes and downgrades nothing, which I confirmed by reading the one-line diff.
2. The comment at :440-441 says the guard is conservative "against the live `.spec/decisions/` tree (dozen+ files today)". The real count is 51. "Dozen+" is true but understates by 4x; a future reader calibrating N off that comment would under-tighten. One-word fix, not worth a bounce.
3. Behaviour change worth knowing at review time: because the capture class is `[a-z_/]+` followed by `\b`, a marker naming a malformed token (digits, uppercase) is now unmatchable rather than partially matched, so it grants no exemption and the token is reported as an unknown code. This fails closed and is backstopped by the existing no-digits invariant test, but an author who writes such a marker will get "unknown finding code" rather than a marker-specific message.
4. Pre-existing and unchanged by this diff (verified identical under both grammars): if a token appears on the same line only inside an ADJACENT plain HTML comment, the sweep counts that as "appears outside the marker" and reports no staleness. That is consistent with the stated contract rather than an evasion of it, and it is not something ozm introduced.

title: Stale-allow-marker sweep has two evasion holes: '>' in reason text defeats the comment strip, and bare unwrapped markers escape the sweep entirely
